page.overview:
What is Thule?

Thule is a legendary land described in Classical Greek literature as being to the far north of Europe. The name was applied to ancient lands in the fiction of Lovecraft Circle writers Robert E. Howard and Clark Ashton Smith, and its role in the Cthulhu Mythos was systematised in the tales of Lin Carter.

Thule was first mentioned by Pytheas, the first documented representative of the Mediterranean world to visit the British Isles. Pytheas' writings do not survive, but he is cited by Strabo as describing Thoulē as an island six days' sail from Britain, near the frozen sea.

The Roman poet Virgil refers in his Georgics to Ultima Thule--"farthest Thule"--which became an expression for any place beyond the known world.

In Smith's "The Double Shadow," a short story published in 1933 and set in the Atlantean remnant of Poseidonis, the narrator Pharpetron wishes that his master, the sorceror Avyctes, "had contented himself with the lore preserved from Atlantis and Thule, or brought over from Mu and Mayapan." He notes that "this should have been enough: for in the ivory-sheeted books of Thule there were blood-writ runes that would call the demons of the fifth and seventh planets, if spoken aloud at the hour of their ascent."
